1000132.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Latin Iuppiter (“Jupiter, the chief Roman god”), also Iūpiter. The Latin nominative continues an ancient vocative expression combining the name of the sky god with pater (“father”), essentially “Father Jove”; compare the oblique stem Iov-, seen in the genitive Iovis.
The name continues Proto-Italic *djous patēr (“sky father”), from *djous (“day, sky”) + *patēr (“father”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dyḗws (“sky; sky god”) and *ph₂tḗr (“father”). The first element belongs to the Proto-Indo-European root *dyew- (“to be bright; day sky”).

1000388.etyen:
Internationalism, ultimately from Ancient Greek Ἔρις (Éris, “Eris, the Greek goddess of strife”), from Ancient Greek ἔρις (éris, “strife, discord”). The deeper origin of the Greek noun is uncertain.
The astronomical sense is named after the goddess. The object was discovered on 5 January 2005 in data obtained on 21 October 2003 by Michael E. Brown, Chad Trujillo and David Rabinowitz. The discovery team proposed the name Eris, which the International Astronomical Union officially assigned on 13 September 2006.
Parallel international forms include Danish Eris, Swedish Eris, German Eris, Dutch Er
